title: One viral key overloads its shard however many shards you add
caption: hash(key) always picks the same shard, so the key's whole request rate lands on one node while the rest idle.

steps.text: A million requests a second arrive, and half of them are for one viral video.
Every request for video:42 hashes to shard 0, which needs ~500k ops/s from a node that does ~100k.
The other shards share the long tail and sit mostly idle: the average looks healthy, the maximum doesn't.
Video:42's neighbours on shard 0 time out too. Going to 8 shards moves video:42 somewhere else, still to exactly one node.

scenarios.name: Celebrity spike
scenarios.summary: A key goes from ordinary to hot in seconds, faster than any autoscaler. Detect hot keys continuously so the mitigation is already switched on.

steps.text: Before: video:42 is one key among millions, and shard 0 runs at 20% like the others.
A celebrity shares it. Within ten seconds its rate goes from 100/s to 500 000/s.
Shard 0 saturates. New shards would take minutes to add and wouldn't help this one key anyway.
Defence: sample request keys (top-k counting) on the router or clients, flag a key once it passes a threshold, and route it to a local cache or split copies.

scenarios.name: Shard 0 dies
scenarios.summary: The overloaded shard fails, its replica is promoted, and the same hot key overloads the replica too: the failure moves, it doesn't end.

steps.text: Shard 0 runs out of CPU and stops answering health checks.
Every key on shard 0 is now failing, not just video:42: the innocent neighbours are hurt most.
Its replica is promoted and receives the same 500k ops/s, so it falls over next. Client retries make it worse.
Fix the cause, not the node: absorb the key before it reaches the shard (local cache, coalescing) and cap retries with backoff.
